clinician.trajectory_summary: A young man in his 20s presented with 4 days of fever (38.7°C), chills, headache, vomiting, and back pain, along with a painless rash on the right occipital region. Despite treatment with cefditoren pivoxil, symptoms persisted. On admission, he had no nuchal rigidity or jolt accentuation, with normal mental status and neurological examination. Lumbar puncture revealed clear, colorless CSF with lymphocyte predominance and atypically low glucose (28 mg/dL). MRI showed no abnormal intracranial signals. Empiric therapy with IV acyclovir (10 mg/kg q8h) and ampicillin was initiated. During hospitalization, the occipital rash evolved with worsening exudate and pain, and dermatology diagnosed herpes zoster based on nature, distribution, and associated pain. Blood and CSF cultures were negative, leading to discontinuation of ampicillin. VZV PCR performed on residual CSF detected VZV DNA at 11×10^6 copies/mL, confirming VZV meningitis. After 5 days of IV acyclovir, fever resolved and symptoms improved; the patient was discharged on oral valacyclovir 1000 mg TID for 5 days.
